name: GlassJelly
overview: Liquid Glass theme for the Jellyfin web client.
description: Apple-style Liquid Glass for jellyfin-web: clear glass capsules and panels that bend what is behind them, an ambient background from the artwork, glass buttons, menus, dialogs, player and dashboard. No Custom CSS needed; a settings page turns the logo, ambient background, hover light and player tweaks on or off.

versions.changelog:
- One material: every glass control and surface uses the header capsule's glass (section 21t). Play / Resume (details
  page and Media Bar) are clear header glass with a white label instead of milky white; the round buttons next to them,
  poster and episode beads, toolbar, pickers, link pills and login buttons share the header's fill, gentle lens and
  rim. Menus, action sheets, dialogs, panels, the player OSD, the now-playing bar, toasts and dashboard cards keep a
  darker tint for long text but use the same rim (one ring + top-left bevel, no doubled arcs at rounded ends).
- Selected and hover states match the header's selected tab and hover everywhere (menu items, sidebars, segmented
  controls, Media Bar settings tab, plugin tabs, picker options).
- Fixes: player OSD buttons no longer carry a lens inside the panel; filter popover sections are no longer grey slabs;
  the poster play bead has no blur at rest on every card; the login buttons' lens and the full-width Cancel now apply.

- Plugin: new option **Subtitle lift** (off by default). While the player controls are visible, subtitles rise just
  above them (the bar height is measured live, so it is right at any resolution) and settle back when they hide; the
  Subtitle Appearance dialog applies to every subtitle type, ASS/SSA included. It sets every user's subtitle styling to
  "Custom", hence opt-in. Per device: `localStorage.jfSubGap` (px above the bar, default 20) and
  `localStorage.jfSubRest` (px at rest, default -1). Script: `src/js/sublift.js`.

- GlassJelly is installable from Jellyfin's plugin catalog: add
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlorinCamarut1/glassjelly/main/manifest.json` in Dashboard → Plugins → Manage
  Repositories, then install GlassJelly. Every release tag builds the plugin on GitHub Actions and adds it to the
  manifest, so updates show up in the dashboard.
- The plugin has its own image in the catalog and the plugin list.
